narr: As the remains of Tropical System Francine slowly meandered through the mid South, a persistent band of showers and thunderstorms produced very heavy rainfall totals over the two day period from the 13th into the 14th. Some of the heaviest rains occurred during the evening of the 13th into the morning hours of the 14th in parts of northwest and north central Alabama. Widespread rain totals of 2 to 4 inches were observed, with a large pocket of 4 to 6 inch rainfall across portions of Cullman, Colbert, Franklin, Lauderdale, Lawrence, and Morgan. A smaller pocket of 8 to 12 inch rainfall was observed in Lawrence Cunty, including the Bankhead National Forest. During the evening hours of the 13th, a few instances of flash flooding weres reported in Cullman County. During the late night and morning hours of the 14th, significant flash and areal flooding occurred as a result in the town of Moulton and nearby areas where several homes were affected by flood water. Small stream and creek flooding persisted through the 15th as runoff fed into the Big Nance Creek which went into Major Flood during the morning hours. A man was rescued from flood waters during the early morning hours of the 15th just south of Courtland near a creek feeding into Big Nance Creek.
